title: Encyclopaedia Britannica online (war and treaty articles)
coverage: Names, dates, parties, and treaty identities that standard references agree on
notes: Default frame for rows whose source_ids are only GENERAL. Rows with a BRITANNICA-* id are the Britannica articles opened on this date. This is not a claim that every row was re-checked in a specialist monograph.

title: History of the Wars
coverage: Gothic War: devastation of Italy with no casualty census
notes: Named as the kind of evidence that survives. Battle figures in Procopius are not used as a body count. No transcription was made for this catalogue.

title: Royal Frankish Annals (Annales regni Francorum)
coverage: Saxon Wars and the Verden entry for 782
notes: The 4500 executions are the usual reading of the 782 annal for one event. Wording and reliability are debated. The Latin was not re-transcribed for this catalogue.

title: De moribus et actis primorum Normanniae ducum
coverage: Grant of land to Rollo
notes: The 911 settlement is known from later narrative. No treaty text survives.

title: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle
coverage: Great Heathen Army
notes: Narrative frame. The written Alfred-Guthrum treaty is a separate document from the baptism at Wedmore.

title: Synopsis Historion
coverage: Kleidion and the claim that 15000 prisoners were blinded
notes: Entered as a chronicle claim. The catalogue does not adopt the number as a fact.

title: Carmen miserabile
publisher_or_project: eyewitness account of the 1241 Hungarian campaign
coverage: Mongol invasion of Hungary
notes: Describes killing and flight. It is not a casualty census.

title: Treaty of Brétigny
coverage: Ransom of John II at three million gold crowns
notes: Opened 2026-11-16. The crowns correspond to the écus of treaty summaries.

title: Treaty of Cambrai
coverage: Ladies' Peace and the ransom of two million écus for Francis I's sons
notes: Tertiary summary opened 2026-11-16. Some popular accounts give a different sum. This catalogue follows the treaty article.

title: Peace of Thorn (1411)
coverage: Collective ransom of 100000 kopas of Prague groschen
notes: Consistent with the obligation letter discussed by Pelech and Ekdahl. A prisoner ransom, not a modern state indemnity.

title: Second Peace of Thorn (1466)
coverage: Royal Prussia and the Teutonic Order as a Polish fief
notes: Territorial and homage terms. No large cash ransom of the 1411 type.

title: Treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton
coverage: Recognition of Scottish independence and a disputed money clause
notes: The money is reported as 20000 pounds and also in other sums, including a National Records of Scotland summary of 100000 pounds. The catalogue does not pick one figure.

title: Treaty of Berwick (1357)
coverage: David II ransom of 100000 merks
notes: Oxford Reference agrees the ransom was 100000 marks. Payments lapsed after the early instalments.

title: Treaty of Stettin (1570)
coverage: Älvsborg ransom of 150000 riksdaler
notes: A further payment to Lübeck is given as 75000 daler here and about 70000 daler in a Swedish overview. The war row records both.

title: Peace of Westphalia
coverage: Swedish satisfaction of five million thalers and the main territorial clauses
notes: The five million thalers also appear in Encyclopedia.com and History Atlas summaries. Payment was slow and Swedish troops remained until it was met.

title: The Thirty Years War: Europe's Tragedy
coverage: Demographic loss in the Holy Roman Empire
notes: Used through the publisher summary and a review quoting Wilson on a population decline of roughly 15 to 20 percent, with regional variation, and estimates of 6 to 8 million deaths. Those figures include disease and hunger. They are not a count of soldiers killed.

title: Why the Armada failed (summary of Martin and Parker, Armada)
coverage: 1588 fleet size and losses on the return
notes: About 130 ships, 2431 guns and 30000 men. About one third of the ships and one half of the men were lost on the return, from wreck, hunger, thirst and the killing of survivors. This is the 1588 voyage, not the whole war of 1585-1604.

title: Truce of Zsitvatorok, document translation
author_or_editor: German History in Documents and Images
coverage: One-time gift of 200000 florins in the translated text
notes: The Hungarian and Ottoman texts have been read differently on whether the payment was strictly once. The catalogue records that split. GHDI's note links the earlier annual tribute to the 1533 peace.

title: Peace of the Pyrenees
coverage: Territorial cessions and the unpaid dowry attached to Maria Theresa's renunciation
notes: The short article confirms an unpaid dowry and does not state the sum. The figure of 500000 gold écus is the usual diplomatic account, including Luis Ribot, and the war row marks it as that account.

title: Treaty of Carlowitz
coverage: 1699 territorial settlement
notes: The catalogue follows the Habsburg gain as Hungary except the Banat, Transylvania, and Croatia-Slavonia. It does not treat the hereditary Slovenian lands as an Ottoman cession of 1699.

title: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
coverage: Territory, navigation, and the Orthodox clause
notes: The short article foregrounds territory and representation. The indemnity is taken from OTTOMAN-KAYNARCA.

title: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca, terms summary
coverage: Indemnity of 15000 purses, stated as 4.5 million rubles, in three instalments
notes: The same sum is repeated in Ottoman-facing summaries. Russian annexation of Crimea in 1783 is a sequel, not a clause of 1774.

title: Treaty of Nystad
coverage: Cessions and a payment of two million silver riksdaler
notes: The Presidential Library of Russia phrases the same sum as two million efimok. The coin name varies. The amount does not.

title: Treaty of Polyanov
coverage: 1634 peace
notes: The Władysław IV summary says 200000 rubles. English Wikipedia says 20000 rubles in gold. The catalogue leaves the sum unresolved.

title: Treaty of Polyanovka
coverage: 1634 peace
notes: Used together with BRITANNICA-POLYANOV to document the conflicting sum.

title: Going to the Wars; This Seat of Mars
coverage: Death estimates for the Wars of the Three Kingdoms, as discussed in a review of the later book
notes: Not used as an adopted total. The review records that Carlton revised his own earlier figures and that the Ireland estimate had been criticised as too high.
